correctness.rationale: Zero divergence gives the graph of the cyclic difference D. Conjugating and averaging over the dihedral signed edge permutations keeps range in this graph and fixes it pointwise, so it still projects and its norm does not grow. Rotation reduces both column types to translates; reflection of a spoke column forces b_k=−b_{n−1−k}; applying the projection to (x,Dx) forces a=δ₀−Db. Conversely those data give a projection, and its norm is the larger of the two graph-column ℓ₁ norms. For 4 and 5 the stated linear kernels both give 2−1/(n−1). For n≥6 the sparse a has mass 1 and cyclic variation 4/5, while b has mass 3/5 and variation 6/5. For the lower bound the coefficient box inequality is valid termwise; after substituting a its linear part pairs a symmetric residual with antisymmetric b and vanishes. A fresh exact calculation on the four displayed rows recovered c=15,21,9,9 with exactly the stated residuals and matching norms. For the unlimited template, u+D*v begins [9,3,2,1], has zero middle, and ends [1,0,3]; substituting it with w+D*z gives [0,1,−1,1,0,…,0,1,−1,1,0], valid also when the middle is empty. This proves the unrestricted norm, not just the finite tested sizes.
